take_homes: Default to one agent. Splitting needs a reason (access, dialect or stance), and the test is whether one prompt could do the same job.
More agents is not more assurance. It means more cost and more handoffs where numbers get lost.
Nothing in this module checks whether the output is true. Anything touching finance needs a human approval step.

monday.move: Ask the controller to try the month-end variance commentary with one agent, as a draft only, with no write access.
monday.who: Controller, with me reviewing the output
monday.when: Next month-end close, not this week
monday.stop_condition: If the draft has any number that doesn't tie to the ledger, or IT says no, we stop.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data.

misconception.why: The module never gave a cost, a payback or a before-and-after, so AI still looks like a licence I buy. The 'one agent is the default' and 'does not check whether the briefing is true' lines made me more careful. They did not show me a capability the organisation builds.

one_line: Sensible on when not to use six agents, but after a day I still have no number for the board, and the answer isn't known to be right.
